$comment: The run-end fault matrix (E28 item 1). Rule: every step of ending a run is repeatable; a step repeated after a partial failure writes the same facts it would have written the first time. For each way a run can end in slice 2 (`endings`) and each store transaction on that ending's path (`faults`), a one-shot fault is armed on the transaction and the run must reach, without a restart, the same final durable facts as the same ending with no fault. A transaction is named by an event it writes (SEAM.md §7, the `before_event` fault): D1 §12.1 has every change write its event in the same transaction, so every transaction on these paths writes an event that D1 A.6 names. The event types are the ones D1 §§3.5, 3.6, 4.1, 4.3, 4.5 and 10 give the facts each ending writes (SEAM.md §§15, 16, 24); they are not read from the engine. Where an engine commits two of them in one transaction, two cells arm the same transaction; where it splits them, each cell arms its own. `stage` says when the fault is armed: `before_end` (default) is the last moment before the test causes the end; `quarantined` is after the run has been quarantined and before termination is observed; `committed` is after the run's commit has been finalized and before its integration is journaled (the barrier journal.commit_tree.finalizer_committed). The endings marked `through: integration` were added by the second slice-3 session (SEAM.md §48): they pass through a commit or an integration, are generated into a file of their own, and carry `operations` (the run's journaled operations and their statuses, in order) and `commits` (what the integration branch gained) in `expect`. `expect` is what the ending leaves whatever the fault: the run's outcome and reason class, whether its invocation is recorded as launched, its workspace's disposition, and the work item once the project has gone on (`work`). `next` is what the project's next item reaches afterwards. Tests generate one separately reported case per fault through ../harness/endings.mjs.

retry.$comment: How long a faulted ending is given (SEAM.md §16, 'The run lease', the safety net; §24). The engine retries a failed step itself. The test waits `wait_ms`; if the run has not ended it then gives the engine, up to `rounds` times, a clock step of two thirds of lease_ttl (shorter than lease_ttl, so nothing expires merely because the clock moved, and together longer than lease_ttl, so the lease that nothing renews any more expires), a tick, and `wait_ms` again.
